title: 2006 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 14
statement:
Find the prime factorization of

\[2006^{2} \cdot 2262-669^{2} \cdot 3599+1593^{2} \cdot 1337\]

(No proof is necessary.)

solutions.text: Upon observing that \(2262=669+1593,3599=1593+2006\), and \(1337=\) \(2006-669\), we are inspired to write \(a=2006, b=669, c=-1593\). The expression in question then rewrites as \(a^{2}(b-c)+b^{2}(c-a)+c^{2}(a-b)\). But, by experimenting in the general case (e.g. setting \(a=b\) ), we find that this polynomial is zero when two of \(a, b, c\) are equal. Immediately we see that it factors as \((b-a)(c-b)(a-c)\), so the original expression is a way of writing \((-1337) \cdot(-2262) \cdot(3599)\). Now, \(1337=7 \cdot 191\), \(2262=2 \cdot 3 \cdot 13 \cdot 29\), and \(3599=60^{2}-1^{2}=59 \cdot 61\).
